title: "4 · Digital quantum circuits"
code-tools: false

![](../assets/thumbs/ch04.png){width=60% fig-align=center fig-alt="Digital quantum circuits"}

Quantum gates are small unitaries on one or two qubits, which makes a quantum circuit a special case of the engine
of Chapter 3. The first notebook introduces rotations as exponentials of Pauli matrices, the standard gate set,
circuits as data that can be compiled with `jit`, circuit identities, and a Trotter step written as a circuit.

The second notebook turns to randomness: Haar-random states and unitaries, the Porter–Thomas distribution of output
probabilities, random brick-wall circuits and the growth of their entanglement, the single-qubit Clifford group,
and cross-entropy benchmarking of random circuit sampling.

## Notebooks in this chapter

::: {.nb-item}
[Quantum gates and circuits — the digital viewpoint](../ch04_digital_quantum_circuits/09_quantum_gates_and_circuits.ipynb)

Qubits are spins and gates are small unitaries: rotations as exponentials of Pauli matrices, circuits as lists of einsum contractions, jit-compiled circuits, circuit identities, a Trotter step as a circuit, and noisy circuits on the density tensor.
:::

::: {.nb-item}
[Random unitaries and random circuits](../ch04_digital_quantum_circuits/10_random_unitaries_and_random_circuits.ipynb)

Haar-random states and unitaries (Mezzadri's QR recipe and why its phase fix matters), the Porter-Thomas distribution, random brick-wall circuits and the growth of entanglement to the Page value, the single-qubit Clifford group, random circuit sampling and cross-entropy benchmarking.
:::
